According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report also further revealed design details of this much-anticipated smart home hub device.

Bloomberg pointed out that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square display, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — its base has a semi-circular arch shape, with a metal stand supporting the screen.

According to Mark Gurman, the device's thickness is "roughly similar to an iPhone," with bezels of about a quarter inch in black, similar to older iPads. The body features a rounded design with "no sharp edges whatsoever."

Below are more design details from the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard gray aluminum casing," with a "rubber bottom that helps it stay firmly placed on a table."
  • It is powered via a USB-C port, with no built-in battery, so it must be connected to a power source at all times.
  • The base is a "circular metal design with multi-ring arranged speaker openings."
  • The display is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the display forward or backward.
  • There are no volume or power buttons on the device.
  • There is a FaceTime camera on the front, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentioned that this home hub has a second version "designed specifically for wall mounting," also powered by USB-C, with a "slim square base containing speakers and microphones" below the display, which reportedly "mounts flush against the wall directly below the screen."

Head over to Bloomberg to read the full report. What do you think of Apple's home hub product? Are you planning to buy one (or more)? Let us know in the comments.
